facts.statement: The genus Glikmanius was named in honor of Russian paleontologist Dr. Leonid Glikman, who was the first to suggest its relationship to ctenacanthiforms.
facts.quote: Glikmanius is named in honour of the Russian palaeontologist, Dr. Leonid Glikman, who studied the genus and was "the first to propose its ctenacanthiform affinity".

facts.statement: Glikmanius is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the order Ctenacanthiformes.
facts.quote: Glikmanius is an extinct genus of ctenacanth cartilaginous fish

facts.statement: Glikmanius lived during the Carboniferous and Permian periods in North America and Russia.
facts.quote: Glikmanius is an extinct genus of ctenacanth cartilaginous fish which lived in the Carboniferous and Permian of North America and Russia.

facts.statement: Skeletal remains of Glikmanius have been found in Nebraska, USA.
facts.quote: Skeletal remains attributed to the genus are known from Nebraska, USA.

facts.statement: Glikmanius occidentalis may have exceeded 6 meters in length, making it one of the largest marine predators of its time.
facts.quote: G. careforum may have reached lengths of 3 m, while G. occidentalis may have reached lengths of over 6 m, making it one the largest marine predators of its time.

facts.statement: Glikmanius is classified within the class Chondrichthyes, subclass Elasmobranchii, and order Ctenacanthiformes.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia phylum: Chordata classis: Chondrichthyes subclassis: Elasmobranchii ordo: Ctenacanthiformes † genus: Glikmanius †

facts.statement: Glikmanius belongs to the family Ctenacanthidae.
Glikmanius lived between 315.2 and 254.14 million years ago, spanning the Moscovian to Wuchiapingian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Moscovian to Wuchiapingian (315.2 to 254.14 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 2026, Egli described fossils from the Carboniferous Pottsville Formation in Alabama, USA, which include the oldest known record of Glikmanius occidentalis.
facts.quote: A new assemblage of cartilaginous fish fossils, including the oldest record of Glikmanius occidentalis reported to date, is described from the Carboniferous (Bashkirian) Pottsville Formation (Alabama, United States) by Egli (2026).

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Glikmanius is Glikmanius occidentalis, originally described by Leidy in 1859.
Three species are recognized within the genus Glikmanius: G. culmenis, G. myachovensis, and G. careforum.
